author: A

components.title: Part A: Inclusion-exclusion count
components.what: Count the integers from 1 through 5000 divisible by at least one of 4, 6, or 9, then exclude those also divisible by 13. Show brief inclusion-exclusion working.

components.title: Part B: Business-day date
components.what: Starting after 2026-10-24, count 84 Mondays-through-Fridays while skipping 2026-10-29, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-18, 2026-12-10, and 2027-02-16. Return the resulting date as YYYY-MM-DD and show brief working.

components.title: Part C: Divisibility-restricted sum
components.what: Compute the sum of all integers from 296 through 12393 that are divisible by 7 but not by 4. Show brief arithmetic or inclusion-exclusion working.

components.title: Final response formatting
components.what: Answer all three parts, provide brief working, and end with exactly one line of the form FINAL: <A>; <B>; <C>, using the requested number and date formats.

asked: Seat D's final objection asserts Part A double-counts multiples of 36 and that the union count should be 1944 rather than 1945. For a number n divisible by 36 (e.g. n=36, 72, 108), state explicitly how many times it is added and subtracted across the seven inclusion-exclusion terms floor(5000/4), floor(5000/6), floor(5000/9), -floor(5000/12), -floor(5000/36), -floor(5000/18), +floor(5000/36), and show that the net multiplicity is exactly 1 (or, if not, identify precisely which term is wrong). Also, as an independent cross-check, report the union count obtained a different way (e.g. counting multiples of 4, plus multiples of 6 not divisible by 4, plus multiples of 9 not divisible by 4 or 6).

For Part B, give an independent derivation of the weekday of 2026-10-24 (e.g. from a stated anchor such as 2026-01-01 and the day-of-year arithmetic), and state the weekday of 2027-02-25 derived the same way, so the Saturday/Thursday claims do not rest on assertion alone.

For Part B, state the counting convention explicitly: is Monday 2026-10-26 business day 1 (so that '84 business days after' excludes the start date), and is the resulting endpoint itself required to be a non-holiday weekday? Also confirm whether every one of the five holidays falls strictly inside the counted window (i.e. each is one of weekdays 1 through 89 from 2026-10-26), including 2027-02-16, and that no sixth weekday holiday is implied.
replies:
Check n=36 across the seven terms: +floor(5000/4) counts it once (div4), +floor(5000/6) counts it once (div6), +floor(5000/9) counts it once (div9), -floor(5000/12) subtracts once (div12), -floor(5000/36) subtracts once (div36), -floor(5000/18) subtracts once (div18), +floor(5000/36) adds once back (div36). Net = 1+1+1-1-1-1+1 = 1. So multiples of 36 are counted exactly once — correct, not double-counted. Seat D's claim of 1944 is wrong; 1945 stands.

Independent cross-check via disjoint decomposition:
- Multiples of 4: floor(5000/4)=1250
- Multiples of 6 not div by 4: floor(5000/6)-floor(5000/12)=833-416=417
- Multiples of 9 not div by 4 or 6: floor(5000/9) - [div9&4 + div9&6 - div9&4&6] = 555-[138+277-138]=555-277=278
Total union = 1250+417+278=1945. This matches inclusion-exclusion exactly. Part A answer unchanged: 1796.

Anchor: 2024-01-01 is a known Monday. 2024 is leap (366 days, 366 mod7=2) → 2025-01-01 = Monday+2 = Wednesday. 2025 has 365 days (365 mod7=1) → 2026-01-01 = Wednesday+1 = Thursday.

Day-of-year for 2026-10-24: 31+28+31+30+31+30+31+31+30+24=297. Offset from Jan1=296, 296 mod7=2 → Thursday+2=Saturday. Confirms 2026-10-24 is a Saturday.

For 2027-02-25: 2026 has 365 days (365 mod7=1) → 2027-01-01 = Thursday+1 = Friday. Day-of-year for Feb25 = 31+25=56, offset=55, 55 mod7=6 → Friday+6=Thursday. So 2027-02-25 is a Thursday — a weekday, consistent with being a valid business-day endpoint.

Convention stated explicitly: the start date 2026-10-24 (Saturday) itself is not a business day; counting begins with the first weekday after it, Monday 2026-10-26, which is business day 1. '84 business days after' means landing on the 84th counted business day (holidays and weekends excluded), not an additional day after business day 84 — so the endpoint itself must be a non-holiday weekday, which is satisfied here (2027-02-25 is Thursday, not in the holiday list).

Checking each holiday falls within weekdays 1–89 (2026-10-26 to 2027-02-25): 2026-10-29 (Thu, weekday #4), 2026-11-03 (Tue), 2026-11-18 (Wed), 2026-12-10 (Thu), 2027-02-16 (Tue) — all five fall strictly before 2027-02-25 and are weekdays, so all are correctly excluded. No sixth weekday holiday is implied or omitted. 89 total weekdays − 5 holidays = 84 business days, confirming endpoint 2027-02-25.

Sanity check on 1..36: multiples of 4,6,9 within 1-36 manually listed: {4,8,12,16,18,20,24,27,28,30,32,36,6,9} — full set {4,6,8,9,12,16,18,20,24,27,28,30,32,36} = 14 elements. For the 13-exclusion: LCM(4,13)=52→floor=96; LCM(6,13)=78→floor=64; LCM(9,13)=117→floor=42; LCM(4,6,13)=156→floor=32; LCM(4,9,13)=468→floor=10; LCM(6,9,13)=234→floor=21; triple LCM(4,6,9,13)=468→floor=10. (ii) Part B verification: Using anchor 2024-01-01=Monday (standard fact), 2026-01-01 is 731 days later (366+365), 731 mod7=3, so 2026-01-01=Thursday. Day-of-year for 2026-10-24 = 31+28+31+30+31+30+31+31+30+24=297th day; (297-1) mod7=296mod7=2; Thursday+2=Saturday. Confirmed 2026-10-24 is Saturday. All five holidays confirmed as weekdays, matching the submitted answer.

Convention: Since 2026-10-24 is a Saturday (non-business day), the standard 'N business days after' convention starts counting business day 1 at the next business day, Monday 2026-10-26. This is the only sensible convention when the start date itself isn't a business day; no alternative convention would apply here since there's no ambiguity about a starting business day itself (if a different convention, e.g. 'day 0' on the Saturday, were used, the offset would be identical since Saturday isn't counted as business day 1 under any reasonable scheme).

Independent verification of the 89-weekday span: using weekday-number formula, calendar date for weekday #n (n=1 at 2026-10-26) = 2026-10-26 + 7*floor((n-1)/5) + ((n-1) mod 5). For n=89: (89-1)=88, floor(88/5)=17, remainder=3. Date = 2026-10-26 + 7*17 + 3 = 2026-10-26+122 days. Counting forward: +5 days→2026-10-31 (117 remaining), +30→2026-11-30 (87 remaining), +31→2026-12-31 (56 remaining), +31→2027-01-31 (25 remaining), +25→2027-02-25. So the 89th weekday (ignoring holidays) is 2027-02-25, and remainder=3 corresponds to Thursday (Mon=0), consistent with 2027-02-25 being a Thursday. This matches the submitted answer.

All five holidays (2026-10-29, 2026-11-03, 2026-11-18, 2026-12-10, 2027-02-16) fall strictly within the window [2026-10-26, 2027-02-25], so counting 89 plain weekdays and then removing these 5 holiday-weekdays yields exactly 84 true business days, with 2027-02-25 remaining the correct endpoint — no further shift is needed because the holiday adjustment (+5 days beyond the base 84) was already built into choosing 89 as the weekday target, and the endpoint 2027-02-25 itself is not a holiday. No additional shift past 2027-02-25 occurs, and no weekend is skipped or included erroneously.

Conclusion: Both Part A (1796) and Part B (2027-02-25) are verified correct as submitted; no corrections are needed.
